# Alpoe London

> Bespoke jewellery house and luxury watch dealer in Hatton Garden, London EC1N. Engagement rings, wedding rings, diamond jewellery and earrings designed with the client and made to order at our own bench; Rolex, Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet and Cartier authenticated, sourced, sold and bought. Natural and laboratory-grown diamonds. Every precious metal piece hallmarked at the London Assay Office. Open Monday to Saturday, 10:00–18:00.

Alpoe London is a jeweller and watch specialist working out of Hatton Garden, the London street that has been the centre of the British jewellery trade since the nineteenth century. The work splits three ways. First, bespoke commissions: engagement rings, wedding bands, earrings, pendants, chains and bracelets designed with the client and made to order — from a sketch, a photograph, a loose stone or an inherited piece to be remade. Second, an online ring builder that lets someone specify a ring themselves — setting style, diamond shape, carat, metal and UK ring size — and send that specification straight to the workshop. Third, luxury watches: authenticated pre-owned and unworn pieces sourced to order, plus buying and part-exchange with same-day payment. Diamonds are offered both natural and laboratory-grown, and the house position is that neither is the right answer for everyone — the guide below sets out the actual trade-offs rather than steering. There is also a mentorship programme for people entering the watch and jewellery trade.

## Rings and engagement rings, by diamond shape

- [Oval Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/oval-engagement-rings): The ratio to ask for (1.30–1.50), what the bow tie is and why some of one is unavoidable, and why an oval faces up larger than a round of the same weight.
- [Round Brilliant Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/round-brilliant-engagement-rings): 57 or 58 facets, and the only shape GIA awards a cut grade. The most expensive per carat, because cutting a circle wastes the most rough.
- [Emerald Cut Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/emerald-cut-engagement-rings): A step cut — it gleams rather than sparkles, and shows every inclusion. GIA recommends VS2 clarity and G colour or better.
- [Radiant Cut Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/radiant-cut-engagement-rings): A mixed cut, 70 facets — step-cut crown, brilliant pavilion. The most forgiving of the rectangular shapes on colour and clarity.
- [Marquise Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/marquise-engagement-rings): The shape that looks largest face-up for its weight, per GIA. Ratio 1.75–2.25, and the points need V-claws.
- [Cushion Cut Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/cushion-cut-engagement-rings): Chunky versus crushed ice, elongated cushions, and why a cushion faces up smaller than its carat weight suggests.
- [Pear Shaped Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/pear-shaped-engagement-rings): Also called a teardrop. Worn point outwards. GIA's own guides disagree on the ideal ratio, and the page says so.
- [Princess Cut Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/princess-cut-engagement-rings): A square modified brilliant, created in 1981. Hides inclusions well in the corners; faces up smaller than its weight.
- [Asscher Cut Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/asscher-cut-engagement-rings): A square step cut, 58 facets, first cut in 1902. Not the same as a Royal Asscher, which has 74 and is patented.
- [Heart Shaped Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/heart-shaped-engagement-rings): Needs half a carat and above to read as a heart at all, per GIA. Symmetry between the lobes is everything.

## Rings, by metal

- [Platinum Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/platinum-engagement-rings): Why platinum displaces metal rather than losing it when scratched, what 950 fineness means, why density makes it cost more than the gram price suggests, and when white gold is the better choice.
- [White Gold Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/white-gold-engagement-rings): White gold is rhodium-plated and the plating wears through in roughly one to three years — what that means, what the alloy is, the nickel question, and how it compares to platinum.
- [Yellow Gold Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/yellow-gold-engagement-rings): What 9ct, 14ct and 18ct change about colour and hardness, why yellow gold never needs plating, and why it lets you drop a diamond colour grade.
- [Rose Gold Engagement Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/rose-gold-engagement-rings): Copper sets the shade and also makes it harder than yellow gold at the same carat. Why shades vary between makers, why it never fades, and what it means for resizing.

## Rings, by style and stock

- [Engagement & Wedding Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/engagement-and-wedding-rings): Fifteen engagement ring styles made to order in Hatton Garden — solitaire, halo, three-stone, rubover, vintage and more — plus wedding rings and matching bands. Choose the diamond shape, setting, metal and UK size.
- [Ring Builder](https://alpoelondon.com/ring-builder): Design your own engagement ring. Pick the setting, diamond shape, carat, metal and ring size and see the result before it is made.
- [Ready to Ship Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings/ready-to-ship): Finished engagement rings held in Hatton Garden, ready to be sized and sent rather than made from scratch.
- [Rings](https://alpoelondon.com/rings): The hub for all three — made to order, wedding bands, and ready to ship.

## Jewellery

- [Fine Jewellery](https://alpoelondon.com/jewellery): Bespoke and ready-to-wear — engagement rings, wedding bands, earrings, necklaces, pendants, bracelets, statement rings and men's jewellery.
- [Bespoke Commissions](https://alpoelondon.com/bespoke): A one-off piece designed around you and hand-set in Hatton Garden. Natural or lab-grown stones, GIA certified.
- [Earrings](https://alpoelondon.com/jewellery/earrings): Diamond studs, hoops and drops in 18ct gold and platinum, plus how to buy a pair — why carat weight is quoted for the pair and not per stone, why a matched pair costs more than twice a single, what claw, three-claw and rubover settings do to a stone, and which earring backs (screw, alpha, butterfly) are actually secure.
- [Bracelets](https://alpoelondon.com/jewellery/bracelets): Tennis bracelets, cluster and link bracelets, made to your wrist, plus how to buy one — why the box clasp and figure-of-eight safety catch matter more than carat weight, how to size a bracelet from a wrist measurement, and the difference between solid and hollow gold links.
- [Necklaces & Pendants](https://alpoelondon.com/jewellery/necklaces-pendants): Tennis necklaces, rivière necklaces, gold link chains and diamond pendants, plus chain length and where each sits (16, 18, 20, 22 and 24 inch), how to match a chain to a pendant's bail and weight, and the difference between a rivière and a tennis necklace.
- [Men's Jewellery](https://alpoelondon.com/jewellery/mens-jewellery): Signet rings, solid gold Cuban chains, pendants and bracelets for men, plus how to buy them — seal versus decorative signet engraving and why it cannot be changed afterwards, onyx and the other traditional signet stones, why the gram weight is the only reliable way to tell a solid chain from a hollow one, and when 9ct makes more sense than 18ct.

## Watches

- [Luxury Watches](https://alpoelondon.com/watches): Authenticated Rolex, Patek Philippe, Audemars Piguet, Richard Mille, Cartier, Hublot and Omega — live stock and sourced to order.
- [Rolex Watches for Sale in London](https://alpoelondon.com/watches/rolex): Live stock, plus how the model families differ and what to check on a pre-owned example — why the reference matters more than the model, polished lugs, papers and bracelet stretch.
- [Audemars Piguet Watches for Sale in London](https://alpoelondon.com/watches/audemars-piguet): Live stock, plus the Royal Oak lineage — how the 39mm Jumbo differs from the 41mm, what tapisserie is, and why case finishing and the integrated bracelet carry the value.
- [Hublot Watches for Sale in London](https://alpoelondon.com/watches/hublot): Live stock, plus Big Bang versus Classic Fusion, what King Gold is, why the strap and ceramic condition matter, and a straight answer on Hublot depreciation.
- [Omega Watches for Sale in London](https://alpoelondon.com/watches/omega): Live stock, plus the Speedmaster in detail — calibre 1861 versus 3861, Hesalite versus sapphire, why the Reduced is not a Moonwatch, and spotting a redialled vintage Omega.
- [Sell or Part-Exchange](https://alpoelondon.com/sell): Free, no-obligation valuation on a luxury watch or piece of jewellery. Authenticated in Hatton Garden and paid the same day.
- [Sell Your Rolex in London](https://alpoelondon.com/sell/rolex): What moves the number on a Rolex — the reference rather than the model, box and papers, bracelet stretch, service history.
- [Sell Your Patek Philippe in London](https://alpoelondon.com/sell/patek-philippe): A thinner, more informed market than Rolex. Originality and the Extract from the Archives carry unusual weight.
- [Sell Your Audemars Piguet in London](https://alpoelondon.com/sell/audemars-piguet): Royal Oak condition is a category rather than a deduction — bevel sharpness and bracelet stretch decide the price.
- [Sell Your Cartier in London](https://alpoelondon.com/sell/cartier): Watches and jewellery both — Tank, Santos, Ballon Bleu, Love bracelets, Juste un Clou and Trinity.
- [Sell Your Omega in London](https://alpoelondon.com/sell/omega): The maker sellers are most often underpaid for, because the high street prices an Omega as a used watch rather than as a reference.

## Workshop services

- [Workshop Services](https://alpoelondon.com/services): Resizing, repairs and remodelling, done at our own bench in Hatton Garden rather than sent away. Pieces we did not make are welcome.
- [Ring Resizing in Hatton Garden](https://alpoelondon.com/services/ring-resizing): How sizing up (metal added) differs from sizing down (metal removed), why a full eternity ring cannot be resized at all, tension settings and full-band engraving, and why a resize on a hallmarked ring goes back through the London Assay Office — adding metal is permitted within limits, removing it is an alteration, and an improperly repaired article is treated in law as never hallmarked.
- [Jewellery Repairs in Hatton Garden](https://alpoelondon.com/services/jewellery-repairs): Claw re-tipping (the repair that prevents most lost stones), shank replacement, chains, clasps and rhodium replating. Includes an annual claw check and an honest note that every polish removes metal.
- [Remodelling Inherited Jewellery](https://alpoelondon.com/services/ring-remodelling): Resetting an inherited stone into something worn rather than kept in a drawer. What carries over (stones, almost always) and what does not (old gold, which is usually better credited than melted), why old cuts should not be recut, and which pieces are worth more left intact.

## Guides and reference

- [Guides index](https://alpoelondon.com/guides): Everything below, indexed.
- [Buying Jewellery in Hatton Garden](https://alpoelondon.com/guides/buying-jewellery-in-hatton-garden): Whether Hatton Garden is really cheaper for an engagement ring and why, the three cases where it is not, how three hundred jewellers came to share a few streets, and what to ask before buying. Historical figures cited to London Museum.
- [What Wedding Band Goes With Your Engagement Ring](https://alpoelondon.com/guides/wedding-bands): Which shapes take a plain straight band, which three usually need one cut to fit, band profiles, width, metal matching and whether to solder the pair.
- [Natural vs Lab-Grown Diamonds](https://alpoelondon.com/guides/natural-vs-lab-grown-diamonds): A laboratory-grown diamond is a diamond, with essentially the same chemical composition, crystal structure and physical properties as a mined stone (ISO 18323). What actually differs, what each costs, how both are graded, and how to choose between them.
- [Where to Propose in London](https://alpoelondon.com/guides/where-to-propose-in-london): Twelve London proposal spots with an honest read on each — Primrose Hill, Kyoto Garden, St Dunstan in the East, Parliament Hill, Richmond Park, Greenwich, Little Venice, Postman's Park, the Sky Garden, Battersea Park, Kew and Hatton Garden itself. Plus golden-hour timing, a wet-weather plan, where to actually keep the ring, arranging a photographer, and getting the ring size right beforehand. Deliberately carries no opening times or ticket prices.
- [Where to Sell a Luxury Watch in London](https://alpoelondon.com/guides/selling-a-luxury-watch-in-london): The six routes compared — dealer, auction, consignment, private sale, instant-buy platform and part-exchange — with what each pays, what it costs in fees and how long it takes. Also what moves the number (reference over model, papers by maker, why not to polish a watch before selling) and the UK tax position for private sellers.
- [Ring Size Guide](https://alpoelondon.com/ring-size-guide): How to measure a ring size accurately at home, the full UK ring size chart A–Z in millimetres with US cross-references, reverse look-up tables converting a circumference or diameter measurement in mm straight back to a UK letter, average UK ring sizes for men and women, four ways to find someone's size without asking, and which rings can and cannot be resized.
- [Hallmarking](https://alpoelondon.com/hallmarking): What the marks struck into a British precious metal piece certify — sponsor's mark, fineness mark and assay office mark — and the statutory Dealer's Notice.
- [Live Metal Prices](https://alpoelondon.com/metal-prices): Gold, silver, platinum and palladium spot prices in GBP and USD, per troy ounce and per gram, with carat breakdowns.
